_why: A small set of facts about the Indian railway timetable that a human verified against a live
source, written down so that our own offline dataset can be tested against reality instead of
against the last build that happened to look plausible.
This is not a data source. It never grows into a schedule: it is 6-8 assertions, and the moment
it needs more than that it is the wrong tool (the fix is a live feed, not a bigger fixture).
Deliberate omissions: NO departure/arrival minutes, and no platform numbers. Those legitimately
differ day to day and revision to revision, so pinning them here would make the gate red for the
wrong reason and train everyone to ignore it. Identity (number -> name -> origin/terminal) and
presence (does a station pair list this train at all) are the two things that do not move under a
passenger's feet and are exactly the two things the app got wrong on 11 Oct 2026.

numbering.why: Five-digit numbers beginning with 0 (06228, 07301, ...) were renumbered out of existence by several zones in 2022-23. A dataset where 10.9% of trains still carry them predates that revision, whatever its git commit date says - so the ETL must not describe freshness by commit date alone.

_pending: must_not_include is empty on purpose. The gate supports phantom-train checks (a service we show that the railway does not run on the pair), and the obvious first entry was 06228 - we list 'SHIMOGA MYSORE EXPRESS 22:10->07:00' on SMET->MYS while the live source listed 16228 there. But 0-prefixed numbers are still used by some zones for festival/special trains, so 'we show a retired number' is not yet proof of 'this train does not exist'. The evidence that would close it is one live pair answer for SMET->MYS (the CI probe or a device log). Until then the honest state is 'suspected phantom', recorded in STATUS, not asserted in a fixture - fabricating a fact to make a test green is the failure mode this whole file exists to stop.
